unit.title: Addition and Subtraction (2)
unit.blurb: Adding and subtracting fractions with the same denominator and with denominators that are multiples of each other.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Add fractions with the same denominator, or where one denominator is a multiple of the other.

O2.t: Subtract fractions with the same denominator, or where one denominator is a multiple of the other.

p: When the denominators are the **same**, add the numerators: 2/7 + 3/7 = **5/7**. The size of the parts does not change.
If one denominator is a multiple of the other, change one fraction first: 1/2 + 1/4 = 2/4 + 1/4 = **3/4**.

lesson.t: Why we need a common denominator
p: We can only add parts of the same size. Changing 1/2 into 2/4 makes it quarters, so it can be added to other quarters.

prac.prompt: Is each statement always, sometimes or never true?

rows.l: Taking a fraction away from 1 leaves less than 1
The answer to a subtraction of two fractions can be simplified

prac.reason: Taking something away from 1 leaves less than 1. The denominator stays 5: 3/5 − 1/5 = 2/5. 5/6 − 2/6 = 3/6 = 1/2 can be simplified, but 3/5 − 1/5 = 2/5 cannot.
